metric_name: Functionally competing foreign arrangement remains less transparent and less comparable
analysis_note: Official factchecks still do not reveal a precise foreign-platform rate formula, but they do strengthen the narrower claim that foreign arrangements are less transparent and less directly comparable to the published domestic tariff and ordinary settlement workflow.

metric_name: Published monthly streaming tariff uses gross-sales base
analysis_note: The published tariff defines monthly streaming revenue as gross sales including discounted amounts, so domestic online-music services remain directly exposed to a published gross-sales rule.

metric_name: Simple domestic-gross versus foreign-net slogan is not fully documented as a one-line formula gap
analysis_note: Factcheck reconfirmed that the strongest defensible reading is not a universal one-line domestic-gross versus foreign-net formula gap, but a transparency and comparability asymmetry between a published domestic tariff and less publicly comparable foreign-platform arrangements.

metric_name: YouTube Music standalone price as a share of full YouTube Premium bundle price
analysis_note: YouTube Music standalone is 0.805 of the full Premium bundle price; the implied music component is KRW 6400, which is 26.4% below Melon's streaming-club price, while the full bundle is 13.3% cheaper than combining Premium Lite with Melon.

metric_name: Korean competition authority required structural relief for YouTube bundle design
analysis_note: The official FTC record says fair competition and consumer choice in the Korean online-music market needed to be restored through structural relief, including a video-only YouTube Premium Lite option.

metric_name: Official audit identifies trust-management governance and budget-control problems
analysis_note: The official MCST audit is described as having found multiple conflict-of-interest, budget-execution, and organizational-operation problems across the music trust-management bodies, which weakens institutional trust and makes foreign-platform disputes harder to verify cleanly.

metric_name: Separate YouTube residual-royalty claim administration signals persistent settlement opacity
analysis_note: The YouTube residual-claim portal now supports only a narrower reading: some YouTube-related settlement requires extra claims and verification workflow. That can complicate transparency and comparability, but the portal does not by itself prove unfair rates or misconduct.

metric_name: Billboard rule change reduced valid repeat downloads from four to one
analysis_note: Billboard-related rule changes are now coded as a partial export-facing metric-dependence signal rather than direct anti-K-pop proof. The strongest reading is that foreign-owned metric design weakened channels where K-pop had been relatively strong, while several alternative explanations remain open.

metric_name: Luminate added Melon and FLO to the Republic of Korea panel in 2023
analysis_note: Luminate's 2023 year-end report says Melon and FLO were added to the Republic of Korea streaming-data panel during 2023. This does not remove foreign metric dependence, but it directly weakens a blanket story that Korean music data are simply excluded from the foreign scoreboard system.

metric_name: No usable Korea-facing tax observation for Alphabet/YouTube Music in current executable firm-quarter panel
analysis_note: Current executable-panel missingness supports only a Korea-facing tax visibility gap, not a blanket nonpayment claim. The metric therefore remains in v2 at a much lower weight as a limited transparency signal.

metric_name: Korean law does not leave foreign digital platforms fully outside VAT and corporate-tax reach
analysis_note: The official Korean tax rulebook confirms that foreign digital platforms are not categorically outside Korea's VAT and corporate-tax reach. This does not make Korea-facing tax incidence fully observable, but it does weaken any blanket narrative that foreign music platforms are simply untaxed in Korea.

metric_name: Matched FY2025 effective tax rate gap between Korean streaming anchor and global peer
analysis_note: Within the same streaming peer and fiscal year, Dreamus/FLO records an effective tax rate of 0.384669 versus Spotify's 0.005396, a gap of 0.379273. This is not a Korea-market tax remittance measure, but it is the strongest directly matched tax-burden gap currently observable in the music peer set.

metric_name: Direct cost panel assigns full tax burden score to Korean anchor and zero to global peer
analysis_note: The direct-cost tax score gap still points in the same direction as the matched FY2025 Dreamus-versus-Spotify effective-tax-rate gap, but it is a second-stage burden score and therefore receives lower support weight than the underlying matched ETR calculation.
